rationale: The previous receipt showed the direct construction repairing node 5 instead of leaving it stuck: after the periodic resend, node 5 ended at accepted 3 and decided 3 with one Prepare and one AcceptSync, while the single Decide it received carried sequence counter 7. That result is counterevidence to the stronger claim that a stable leader has no repair path, but the receipt did not show the order in which those messages arrived or what each one did to node 5's accepted and decided indices, so it cannot yet say whether the Decide was processed (and clamped) or rejected as a sequence break. This revision keeps the construction and comparison identical and pumps node 5's inbound Paxos messages one at a time, recording a bounded ordered trace of message kind, sequence counter and the local (accepted, decided) pair before and after each message.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds a bounded ordered trace of the Paxos messages delivered to node 5 during the 150 tick-driven resend rounds, with the message kind, sequence counter, and node 5's (accepted, decided) pair before and after each message. The construction, ready admission event, comparison and final fields are unchanged.

scope.description: Five OmniPaxos instances over MemoryStorage with an explicit message pump. Node 1 is made leader with try_become_leader, appends and decides entries 1..2 on every node, then reconfigures to configuration_id 2. The AcceptStopSign addressed to node 5 and the leader's subsequent Decide addressed to node 5 are discarded; all other traffic is delivered until quiescent. Every node is then ticked 150 times with election_tick_timeout 1000 and resend_message_tick_timeout 100, delivering all messages, so only tick-driven resends can reach node 5. Within each tick the pump runs to quiescence and delivers node 5's inbound Paxos messages one at a time so their order and local effect can be recorded.
assumptions: Node 5 has already accepted and decided entries 1..2 before the reconfiguration, so its only missing log position is the StopSign.

Discarding the AcceptStopSign and the first Decide to node 5 models a follower that misses both the StopSign acceptance and the initial decision notice while remaining connected and promised to the leader.
election_tick_timeout 1000 keeps leadership stable across the 150 ticks, and resend_message_tick_timeout 100 guarantees at least one leader resend inside that window.
excluded: Leadership changes, reconnected() calls, snapshots, trimming, batching, flexible quorums and starting the next configuration.

experiment.prefix: Fresh harness functions build_node_slow_election (same five-node configuration_id 1 cluster, election_tick_timeout 1000, resend_message_tick_timeout 100), is_stopsign_to, settle_without_stopsign_to, decide_seq and msg_tag; the test decided_stopsign_only_decide_is_resent settles the empty cluster, calls try_become_leader on node 1, appends Value(1) and Value(2) with a full settle after each, emits the ready event, calls reconfigure to configuration_id 2, then settles while discarding AcceptStopSign and Decide messages addressed to pid 5. It then ticks every node 150 times; inside each tick it pumps to quiescence, delivers the queued messages addressed to pid 5 one at a time, appends at most ten Paxos messages to a trace as kind+sequence counter and node 5's accepted-decided pair before and after the delivery, and routes the remaining messages. It emits after_resend with node 5 accepted/decided/leader/promise state, the leader's decided index, decision_gap, Decide/Prepare/AcceptSync/AcceptStopSign counts and the last Decide sequence counter, and the joined trace.

comparisons.description: Bounded convergence after the decision: a follower that had accepted entries 1..2 and missed only the StopSign is at the leader's decided index after 150 ticks, during which the leader resent at least one Decide to it.
